episodes.212595: During the 9th evening, a moist and unstable airmass across central Indiana interacted with an approaching upper-level disturbance resulting in severe thunderstorms. Thunderstorms initially developed in western and northwestern central Indiana after 6:00 PM EST before organizing into line segments that tracked eastward across the region through the late evening and overnight hours.||Strong straight-line wind gusts were produced by the severe thunderstorms. Peak measured wind gusts reached 61 mph at the Purdue University Airport in Tippecanoe County and 63 mph at the Indianapolis Regional Airport in Hancock County. The severe winds caused broad impacts across Tippecanoe, Vigo, Clay, Morgan, Hendricks, Hancock, and Johnson counties, primarily consisting of downed trees, large tree limbs, and localized power line damage that created temporary roadway obstructions.||Repeated convective activity and heavy rainfall totals between 2.5 and 4 inches subsequently impacted eastern portions of the area during the early morning hours of June 10. This heavy rain led to localized flash flooding across roadways in Decatur County, though no building inundation or water rescues were reported before floodwaters receded. This severe weather event would be the second of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.
episodes.212615: A band of thunderstorms developed along a surface trough and moved swiftly east during the afternoon hours. This resulted in localized gale-force wind gusts over the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.212620: A shortwave advancing through the Ohio Valley and Pennsylvania allowed for a complex of thunderstorms to develop across western Pennsylvania during the morning hours of June 10, 2026. Upscale growth of this complex continued into portions of central Pennsylvania where slightly more moisture and instability was in place, with CAPE values peaking between 2000-3000 J/kg during the afternoon hours across much of the region. Storms largely stayed below severe limits due to the lack of bulk shear; however, some strong-to-severe thunderstorms knocked down trees in northern York County. Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall occurred during portions of Mifflin County, where ponding of water occurred due to a slow-moving thunderstorm ahead of this complex with additional rainfall occurring during the afternoon hours.
episodes.212630: Multiple thunderstorm cells were observed training across the Flat Rock Community, located just northeast of the town of Mt Airy in Surry County. Cells began crossing the area at around 5:45 pm EDT, and continued passing across the area repeatedly until around 8:15 pm EDT before rainfall became light in intensity. Rainfall rates rose to as high as 5 inches per hour multiple times through the event. Despite dry antecedent conditions with D2: Severe Drought highlighted for the northern half of Surry County by the U.S. Drought Monitor, MRMS FLASH data estimated the rainfall reached the 142-year Average Recurrence Interval ceiling for a 3-hour duration in the Flat Rock area, with rainfall totals reaching 120 percent of the 3-hour Flash Flood Guidance. CREST Unit Streamflow was unimpressive however, reaching into the 300 to 400 cfs per mi^2 by around 8:00 pm EDT. The heavy rain produced runoff around 6 inches deep across Highway 103 from a nearby hillside drainage.
episodes.212636: A cluster of storms initially generated hail mainly to the size of quarters across portions of central South Dakota, then organized into a line and increased speed. This resulted in high winds across northeast South Dakota during the late evening and early overnight hours. A peak wind gust of 90 mph was recorded by the South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) mesonet station 4 miles north of Altamont, with a 78 mph wind gust recorded on a personal weather station 9 miles northwest of Aberdeen, 77 mph on a personal weather station in Faulkton and a 74 mph gust at the SDDOT station near Ree Heights (Hand County). ||Intermittent wind damage was reported across much of northeast South Dakota, with reports of peeled roofs and lost tiles, blown in garages and trees down. In the city of Aberdeen and surrounding area, several of these trees landed on vehicles. The Aberdeen City Forester reported the cost for just tree cleanup on city property (including boulevards) topped out at $14,585. ||Six miles south of Goodwin, multiple irrigation pivots were twisted by intense winds. Major power outages affected 5,849 customers in Brown County, 1,106 in Hamlin County, and 64 in Deuel County.
episodes.212688: The incredible stretch of severe weather continued on Wednesday June 10th with more severe storms and a few small tornadoes across Dickinson county.  The storms also dumped  more flooding rains across parts of Kansas that were already saturated from days of torrential rainfall.
episodes.212860: A line of thunderstorms developed north of a warm front and tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the afternoon on Wednesday (6/10). The strongest storms produced wind damage and severe wind gusts as they tracked through the region.
episodes.212890: An area of thunderstorms produced a bolt of lightning, striking a residence in the Townsend area.  The lightning caused a fire and produced extensive damage to the home, estimated to be around $100,000.
episodes.212897: Thunderstorms continued to produce high winds as they moved out of northeast South Dakota into western Minnesota. Residents 4 miles east northeast of Ortonville reported that a large pine had snapped at the base, with additional tree damage in the area.
episodes.213072: A line of severe thunderstorms that would eventually become a derecho, produced widespread wind damage across much of northeast Illinois during the afternoon of June 10th. Two brief tornadoes also occurred.
episodes.213073: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across northwest Indiana during the afternoon of June 10th, producing severe wind gusts and isolated wind damage.
episodes.213074: A line of thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of June 10th producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.213240: A line of thunderstorms moved from Illinois through southwest Michigan and northern Indiana. The line of storms eventually weakened, but prior to this, damaging wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.213241: A line of thunderstorms moved from Illinois through southwest Michigan and northern Indiana. The line of storms eventually weakened, but prior to this, damaging wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.213453: A few widely scattered showers and storms impacted portions of central Kansas during the evening and nighttime hours of June 9. Some of these storms were severe and produced wind gusts up to 70 mph. These strong wind gusts also contributed to an overturned semi on I-70.
episodes.213487: Several rounds of thunderstorms moved through the region Wednesday and Thursday that brought heavy rain, damaging wind, and several brief tornadoes to eastern IA, northwest IL, and northeast MO.  The more widespread wind damage occurred Wednesday afternoon June 10th from a derecho that developed in eastern Iowa and moved east. This downed trees, power lines primarily along and north of I-80. The more significant winds between 70-80 mph winds were seen north of the Hwy 20 corridor. A second round of storms later on produced isolated wind damage, including some damage north of Geneseo, IL that was due to straight-line winds.
episodes.213488: Several rounds of thunderstorms moved through the region Wednesday and Thursday that brought heavy rain, damaging wind, and several brief tornadoes to eastern IA, northwest IL, and northeast MO.  The more widespread wind damage occurred Wednesday afternoon June 10th from a derecho that developed in eastern Iowa and moved east. This downed trees, power lines primarily along and north of I-80. The more significant winds between 70-80 mph winds were seen north of the Hwy 20 corridor. A second round of storms later on produced isolated wind damage, including some damage north of Geneseo, IL that was due to straight-line winds.
episodes.213601: This episode is part 1 of 2 from two rounds of severe weather that occurred during the late evening of June 9th into the early morning of June 10th. ||Widespread wind damage occurred across western Minnesota during overnight storms which had moved in from the Dakotas. The strongest wind report was observed in Lac Qui Parle County at 83 mph near Marietta, MN. One tornado was caught on camera overnight near the Kandiyohi and Pope County line, but no damage was reported, leaving its rating as EF-U (Unknown). As the line of storms continued east, wind gusts decreased to 30-40kts in most areas. However, several emergency managers areas reported downed trees within their municipalities. A few downbursts did occur northeast of the Twin Cities metro area, with tree damage being reported from St Paul up towards Shoreview and White Bear Lake and then all the way up to Forest Lake and Chisago City.
episodes.213602: This episode is part 1 of 2 from two rounds of severe weather that occurred during the early morning of June 10th.||A line of strong thunderstorms which had caused widespread wind damage across Minnesota continued into western Wisconsin. The strongest wind gusts had decreased as the line of storms progressed across central and eastern MN. However, emergency managers and law enforcement reported downed trees within their municipalities.||Wind damage for this episode was focused across Pierce, Dunn, and Eau Claire Counties. Estimated wind gusts between 50-55kts produced damage to a couple of farm outbuildings just northeast of Rock Elm (Pierce Co). While farther east, several trees and powerlines were downed between Menomonie and Downsville.
episodes.213699: Scattered thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall and flooding during the early morning hours.
episodes.213700: Scattered thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall and flooding during the early morning hours.
episodes.213753: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.213758: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.213805: Moist upslope flow allowed thunderstorms to develop in and around the higher terrain of west Texas, especially near the Davis Mountains. A couple of storms managed to become severe, producing damaging winds in Pecos and Jeff Davis counties.
episodes.214000: On June 10th, an inverted trough over the Atlantic Ocean waters adjacent to the northeast Florida and southeast Georgia waters developed coastal showers that moved onshore in the overnight into morning hours. Showers interacted with the land breeze creating a convergent line of heavy showers that caused flooding along the coast. Moist west-southwest flow then developed resulting in typical summertime sea breeze thunderstorms each afternoon into evening for the next several days. The strongest storms were along the sea breeze collisions near HWY 301 and U.S. Route 23.
episodes.214003: A broken line of thunderstorms formed ahead of an outflow boundary along the Mississippi River around midday on June 10th.  Some of the stronger cells within the line produced 60mph wind gusts and scattered damage along and north of a Jacksonville to Clinton line through mid-afternoon.
episodes.214012: The combination of an overnight/early morning land breeze and weakening back door front over FL waters resulted in a nearly linear area of heavy showers over parts of coastal Northeast FL.
episodes.214146: On June 10th, daytime heating pushed temperatures into the upper 80s and lower 90s, combining with surging humidity to drive heat indices near 100��F and create a highly unstable environment with MLCAPE values reaching 2,500 J/kg. Weak low-level convergence initially triggered severe storms over Wayne County, which dropped 1 to 1.25-inch hail across Dearborn and Dearborn Heights. Later in the evening, a destructive Midwestern squall line tracked into southern Lower Michigan, though it steadily weakened as it moved through Southeast Michigan before completely clearing the state by midnight. While the broader system left over 85,000 customers without power statewide, wind damage, downed trees, and power outages within Southeast Michigan remained isolated to scattered, impacting communities primarily along and west of U.S. 23.
episodes.214237: A cluster of thunderstorms in West Virginia morphed into a weak mesoscale convective system as it crossed the Appalachians and into Virginia. While a mid-level shortwave provided a source of lift, MLCAPE of at least 1,000 J/kg and 20-30 knot bulk shear was just enough to organize storms to deliver damaging wind gusts to the Piedmont of Virginia. The fast nature of the system prevented any flooding for Virginia in spite of anomalously high PWAT values of 1.70-2.00 inches.
episodes.214259: A shortwave trough lifted northeast from the Ohio Valley into the lower Great Lakes during the evening of June 9, 2026 through the early morning hours of June 10, 2026. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a nearly stationary front in southern lower Michigan and intensified across northern Ohio with the approach of the shortwave late in the evening. Thunderstorms with intense rainfall rates slowly moved east across Sandusky County, Ohio with PWAT values near 2 inches and weak deep layer shear. Total rainfall amounts of 2.5 to 4 inches fell across Sandusky County, Ohio over a two to three hour period, with instantaneous rainfall rates of 3 to 5 inches per hour at times.
episodes.214262: A strong thunderstorm moved across the Detroit River, overturning several sailboats.
episodes.214309: During the 10th late afternoon and early evening, a warm, unstable air mass interacting with an approaching upper wave and weak frontal boundary triggered a few severe thunderstorms across central Indiana.  Adequate atmospheric instability and vertical wind shear supported brief cell organization as convective activity tracked eastward across the region.  ||The severe weather event began around 5:50 PM EST in Tippecanoe County, where initial storm development produced isolated severe hail up to 1.00 inch in diameter. As the convection moved eastward into Howard County near 6:55 PM EST, storms produced localized straight-line thunderstorm wind gusts which downed several trees before activity dissipated later in the evening.
episodes.214521: On June 10th, 2026, two distinct rounds of storms impacted northeastern Minnesota. The initial early-morning line of storms brought damaging wind gusts up to 60-65 mph that uprooted trees and knocked out power in a few places. A second round of severe thunderstorms fired up during the afternoon and evening hours, producing localized strong winds, heavy rainfall, and large hail ranging from quarter to half dollar size.
episodes.214522: A few severe thunderstorms occurred across northwestern Wisconsin on the afternoon of the 10th. These storms produced damaging wind gusts resulting in tree damage along with heavy rainfall leading to minor flooding.
episodes.214602: A large-scale mid-level trough nudged out into the Northern Plains while a strong frontal boundary moved out across the Dakotas. Storms initiated with up to 3000 J/kg elevated CAPE near a surface boundary. Storms quickly organized into a linear system with short bowing segments which produced gusts of 60 to 75 mph. A large trailing stratiform precipitation shield developed featuring a strong wake-low an hour or two after the strong thunderstorm outflow winds with gusts up to 70 mph.
episodes.214685: An active stretch of weather took shape across West Virginia from June 10th to the 12th amid several passing disturbances. Beginning on the morning of the 10th, overnight thunderstorm complexes across the Ohio Valley spilled into the state just after sunrise, containing heavy downpours. This resulted in high water issues across isolated spots in Lincoln, Putnam, and Kanawha Counties through the late morning hours before the departure of the first upper level disturbance.||A brief reprieve from the evening of the 10th to the morning of 11th was quickly interrupted by an approaching cold front that promoted diurnally showers and thunderstorms for the next two days. Thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon on June 11th across north-central West Virginia and tracked eastward into the mountains. Damaging winds associated with storms resulted in a swath of downed trees and power lines in these areas before dissipating with the loss of daytime heating. A similar setup took place the next day as the front slid through the forecast area, with storms developing around midday, this time across portions of central and southern West Virginia. More tree and power line damage occurred as a result, along with one instance of one inch hail. The cold front slipped through the entire area by the evening of June 12th, mitigating further showers and storms in the state.
episodes.214852: A large linear MCS progressed west to east across eastern ND during the evening hours of June 9th and early morning hours of June 10th. Severe winds occurred over parts of eastern ND.
episodes.214853: A large linear MCS progressed west to east across eastern ND late on the evening of June 9th and into northwest MN during the early morning hours of June 10th. Severe wind gusts occurred over much of northwest and west central MN during the early morning hours, with one report of quarter size hail.
episodes.214854: A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 60 mph at Cooperstown, ND in eastern ND. Other thunderstorms produced non severe winds and hail over parts of eastern ND.
episodes.214855: Severe thunderstorms develop during the afternoon hours across northwest MN, with reports of severe hail and several reports of wind damage.
episodes.214941: This episode is part 2 of 2 from two rounds of severe weather that occurred on June 10th. ||Two clusters of storms redeveloped across Minnesota during the early afternoon of June 10th. The first cluster developed over Douglas and Stevens Counties and rapidly intensified as it entered Pope County. This cluster produced golf ball to tennis ball size hail in Glenwood and Villard (Pope). This storm would weaken some as it continued to the NNE into Stearns, Todd, and Morrison Counties where a brief funnel cloud was observed just south of Sobieski (Morrison). ||The second cluster of storms developed farther east across eastern MN along the I-35 corridor. A supercell entered Chisago County and produced quarter size to golf ball size from Wyoming to Center City.
episodes.214964: Thunderstorms developed over the southern Nebraska Panhandle and northeastern Colorado during the late afternoon hours of June 9th. As this activity pushed east, it encountered favorable moisture and shear, and became severe. Activity was isolated initially, but became more numerous into the evening hours. Hail up to the size of baseballs was reported in McPherson County while 79 MPH wind gusts were reported in Holt County.
episodes.214965: A surface trough and low-level jet combined with a very moist and unstable air mass that led to severe thunderstorm development along the triple point of a surface low in west central North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon in southwest North Dakota, with additional storms in the far northwest. Storms gradually moved to the north-northeast through the evening in a primarily cluster storm mode. The area of most significant damage was in Ward and McHenry Counties. In the town of Sawyer in Ward County, the Emergency Manager reported damage from powerful thunderstorm wind gusts that resulted in power outages, trees on roads, and a large tree that fell onto a house and made a hole in the roof. Northeast of Deering in McHenry County, there was significant damage to a homestead due to thunderstorm wind gusts. A barn on the property had roof panels ripped off and some collapse of the wood frame structure for the roof. Damage in both of these locations were consistent with wind speeds around 90 mph. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, a few miles west of Fortuna in Divide County. One tornado occurred with these storms, and was reported approximately 3 miles east of Noonan in Divide County. It was a very brief tornado and caused no known damage, so has been rated EF-Unknown by NWS policy.
episodes.214997: Severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds and isolated flash flooding to northern Ohio.
episodes.215009: A few storms across Bennette and Mallette counties produced minor severe weather.
episodes.215035: Multiple rounds of storms on June 10th brought severe wind gusts and isolated large hail to portions of western Wisconsin throughout the day. The most prolific of these rounds was during the afternoon, where wind gusts as high as 85 mph were reported with a bow echo that clipped southern Grant County and continued eastward across southern Wisconsin. This intense complex that was later classified as a derecho by SPC.
episodes.215058: An intense complex of thunderstorms tracked across most of southern Wisconsin, northern Illinois, and portions of northeast Wisconsin during the afternoon hours on June 10, 2026. Multiple measured wind gusts of 70+ MPH were reported as the storms moved across southern Wisconsin, resulting in widespread tree & power line damage. Several areas of structural damage also occurred, with subsequent damage surveys identifying two EF0 tornadoes near the communities of Lomira and Eden. Analysis conducted by the Storm Prediction Center identified the June 10 thunderstorm complex as a derecho.
episodes.215083: Scattered storms moved across southern Virginia during the afternoon of June 10. One storm became severe.
episodes.215084: A line of storms moves across the James River, Chesapeake Bay, and Virginia coastal waters on June 10, producing gusty winds.
episodes.215252: Several supercell thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 10th across portions of central and northeast Kansas. Large hail up to baseball size, damaging winds, and a brief tornado occurred.
episodes.215393: During the evening of June 9, 2026, scattered thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across portions of eastern Nebraska. A warm, unstable air mass fueled the activity as a surface low deepened and moved eastward into the state. Storms initially developed in central Nebraska before tracking east-northeastward, with peak wind gusts measured between 59 and 70 mph across Boone, Antelope, Butler, and Wayne counties. Storm intensity gradually diminished as the system moved northeastward into the late evening.
episodes.215518: On June 10, 2026, a warm front pushing across the NWS Buffalo region tapped into a hot, humid airmass with dewpoints in the upper 60s and 70s, setting the stage for organized summer convection. As a mid-level disturbance tracked over the Great Lakes, multi-cell thunderstorm clusters formed over Western New York and consolidated into linear segments, prompting SPC Severe Thunderstorm risks for damaging wind gusts and hail. Simultaneously, atmospheric precipitable water levels near 1.5 inches triggered localized heavy downpours up to 1.5 inches per hour, leading to WPC Marginal Excessive Rainfall risks and minor urban flooding in low-lying areas. Convective activity waned overnight with the loss of diurnal heating, giving way to cold air advection behind the cold front that fueled early-season lake-induced instability and marine hazards across Lakes Erie and Ontario.
episodes.215602: Severe storms moved through portions of southeast Minnesota during the late afternoon hours resulting in sporadic instances of severe hail and damaging wind gusts, primarily in Olmsted and Winona counties.
episodes.215639: This episode is part 2 of 2 from two rounds of severe weather that occurred on June 10th. ||A second line of thunderstorms developed along the I-35 corridor in eastern MN and tracked northeast into western Wisconsin. The cells within this line had a history of producing ping-pong ball (1.5 inches) size hail in eastern Minnesota, but once they crossed the St. Croix River Valley, the storms had weakened some but still managed to produce dime to quarter size hail in St. Croix Falls (Polk) and Rice Lake (Barron).
episodes.215842: A destructive Midwestern squall line tracked into Lower Michigan on June 10 resulting in tens of thousands of power outages statewide from wind damage and down trees.
episodes.215845: Severe weather occurred across west Michigan with 2 tornadoes causing damage.
